name: biogears-sbml-sepsis
title: BioGears sepsis core: engine vs SBML extraction

campaign_docs.name: BioGears sepsis core in Antimony: extraction report (Sauro)
campaign_docs.path: investigations/biogears-sbml-sepsis/sources/BioGears sepsis core in Antimony extraction report.pdf

lead:
BioGears is a lumped-parameter C++ whole-body physiology engine. Its sepsis
core — cardiovascular circuit, baroreflex, capillary fluid/albumin exchange,
and the McDaniel 2019 Acute Inflammatory Response — was extracted by Herbert
Sauro into a single Antimony model (91 state variables) that also exports to
SBML. That extraction was validated only against the paper's published
milestones, because the author could not run BioGears. This investigation runs
both: the real engine via viva-biogears and the SBML extraction via
viva-tellurium, side by side, to produce the run-for-run comparison the
extraction report could not.
question:
Does the Antimony/SBML extraction of the BioGears sepsis core reproduce the
real BioGears engine run-for-run — not merely against the McDaniel et al. 2019
paper milestones — and where does it diverge, and why?
hypothesis:
The extraction reproduces BioGears' healthy baseline and the qualitative mild
and severe infection outcomes, but the severe course lags the engine by several
hours and the two diverge on observables fed by processes the extraction does
not translate (urine, fever-driven vasodilation, lactate, intracellular water).

executive.what_is_this:
A side-by-side comparison of the BioGears sepsis core run two ways — the real
BioGears 8.2.0 engine (viva-biogears) versus its SBML/Antimony extraction
(viva-tellurium) — across a healthy baseline and mild and severe infection,
plus a runtime axis comparing the Python process-bigraph engine with the Rust
viva-core engine on the same composite.
executive.verdict:
The SBML extraction reproduces the BioGears sepsis core's inflammation almost
exactly but its hemodynamic collapse arrives ~11 h late. Run-for-run over 48 h:
baseline parity holds; mild stays controlled on both sides; under severe sepsis
SBP crosses 100 mmHg at 37.5 h in the extraction vs 26.6 h in the real engine
(a 10.9 h lag), while tissue integrity (0.325/0.325) and pathogen load
(60.5/60.6) match within ~0.1% (tissue integrity to ~1e-4, peak pathogen to ~1e-3). The engine-vs-extraction comparison the extraction
report could not make — confirming and slightly exceeding its ~8-10 h estimate.
executive.verdict_detail:
All four 48 h arms ran (severity 1 & 3 × engine & SBML, locally-built BioGears
8.2.0). Parity gate closed; cross-engine runtime axis bit-identical. The
divergence is confined to the hemodynamic response (the untranslated urine /
fever-vasodilation / lactate / intracellular-water processes), not the
inflammation model. Remaining work is packaging: comparison figures + report,
then publish once org access lands.

scientific_argument.main_claim:
The SBML extraction is a faithful, independently-runnable surrogate for the
BioGears sepsis core at baseline and for qualitative infection outcomes, with
quantifiable, mechanistically-attributable divergence under severe sepsis.
evidence_for: SBML baseline matches BioGears StandardMale targets within tolerance (study 01).
Extraction report: all qualitative mild/severe outcomes reproduced vs McDaniel 2019 milestones.
evidence_against: Report notes the severe course runs ~8-10 h behind BioGears.
Untranslated processes (urine, fever vasodilation, lactate, intracellular water) are known omissions.
caveats: Validation to date is extraction-vs-paper, not extraction-vs-engine; closing that gap is the point of this investigation.
viva-biogears runs its InfectionModerate nutrition schedule; the extraction does not model meals — a documented scenario delta.

competing_frameworks.name: Extraction validated against paper milestones only (status quo)
competing_frameworks.relation: This investigation supersedes it with a run-for-run engine comparison.

studies.name: 01-baseline-parity
studies.title: Baseline parity
studies.question:
At rest (no infection), do the real BioGears engine and the SBML/Antimony
extraction settle to the same StandardMale baseline haemodynamics, so that any
later divergence under infection is attributable to the model and not to a
mismatched starting state?

findings.summary: Engine and SBML baselines match at rest — run-for-run parity holds.
findings.detail:
Real BioGears 8.2.0 (severity 0, 5 min): SBP 114.87, DBP 74.54, HR 72.24,
CO 5.81 L/min. SBML extraction (severity 0, 30 s): SBP 114.6, DBP 73.48,
HR 71.5, CO 5.905 L/min. Max difference ~1 mmHg / ~0.7 bpm / ~0.1 L/min —
well within physiological tolerance. Both read uninfected (blood_pathogen ~0,
tissue_integrity ~1.0). The parity gate PASSES, so divergence under
infection (studies 02/03) reflects the model, not the starting state.

studies.claim:
Both sides hold the BioGears StandardMale baseline and match each other at rest:
real engine SBP 114.9 / DBP 74.5 / HR 72.2 / CO 5.81 L/min vs SBML extraction
SBP 114.6 / DBP 73.5 / HR 71.5 / CO 5.9 L/min — all within physiological
tolerance. The run-for-run parity gate PASSES; infection divergence measured in
studies 02/03 is attributable to the model, not a mismatched starting state.

derived.insight: Engine and SBML baselines match at rest — run-for-run parity holds.

studies.name: 02-mild-infection
studies.title: Mild infection (severity 1)
studies.question:
Under a mild infection (severity 1), does the SBML extraction reproduce the
BioGears engine's course — a controlled infection that resolves without
progressing to hypotension — run for run?

findings.summary: Mild infection stays controlled on both sides; no hypotension milestones crossed.
findings.detail:
Both arms, severity 1, 48 h, infection at t=0: SBP<100, MAP<65 and HR>90 are
never reached (sustained) on either side. tissue_integrity minimum
0.96755/0.96755; peak blood_pathogen 6.2983/6.2983 — near-identical.
Hemodynamics differ over the course (SBP max-abs ~10.6 mmHg, DBP ~5, MAP ~7.6,
HR ~6.3 bpm, blood_volume ~0.57 L, plus a cardiac-output offset), but the qualitative mild outcome agrees run-for-run.

studies.claim:
Under mild infection both the real engine and the SBML extraction keep the
infection controlled over 48 h — neither crosses into hypotension (no SBP<100,
no MAP<65, no HR>90) — and the inflammation core matches almost exactly
(tissue integrity min 0.9676/0.9676, peak pathogen 6.298/6.298). Mild is the
agreement case that frames the severe-arm divergence.

derived.insight: Mild infection stays controlled on both sides; no hypotension milestones crossed.

studies.name: 03-severe-infection
studies.title: Severe infection (severity 3)
studies.question:
Under a severe infection (severity 3), does the SBML extraction track the
BioGears engine's collapse sequence run-for-run, and how large is the known
timing divergence (the extraction report saw the severe course lag by ~8-10 h
against the paper)?

findings.summary: Severe hemodynamic collapse lags the real engine by ~11 h (SBP<100: 37.5 h vs 26.6 h).
findings.detail:
Both arms, severity 3, 48 h, infection at t=0, run-for-run:
- SBP < 100 mmHg: engine 26.55 h, extraction 37.47 h -> +10.9 h lag.
- HR > 90 /min: engine 26.77 h, extraction 37.55 h -> +10.8 h lag.
- MAP < 65 mmHg: neither crossed (sustained) by 48 h.
- SVR ratio minimum: engine 0.952, extraction 0.715 — the extraction
  over-shoots the vasodilation.
The delay most likely comes from processes the extraction does not translate
(urine loss, fever-driven skin vasodilation, lactate, intracellular water).

findings.summary: The inflammation / pathogen core matches the engine almost bit-for-bit.
findings.detail:
tissue_integrity minimum 0.3248 (engine) vs 0.3248 (extraction); peak
blood_pathogen 60.55 vs 60.60 (both are 48 h-horizon values; *_h = 48.0, so the true peak/min is not yet reached). The Acute Inflammatory Response the extraction
copied from BioGears reproduces the engine's dynamics to ~1e-4 for tissue integrity (~1e-3 for peak pathogen); divergence is
confined to the hemodynamic response, not the inflammation model.

studies.claim:
Run-for-run, the SBML extraction reproduces BioGears' severe-sepsis inflammation
almost exactly (tissue integrity 0.325/0.325, peak pathogen 60.5/60.6; values at the 48 h horizon, the severe course not yet at its true peak/min) but its
hemodynamic collapse arrives ~11 h LATE: SBP crosses 100 mmHg at 37.5 h in the
extraction vs 26.6 h in the real engine (a 10.9 h lag), with the same ~11 h lag
on the HR>90 compensation. This is the engine-vs-extraction comparison the
extraction report could not make; it confirms and slightly exceeds its ~8-10 h
estimate against the paper.

derived.insight: Severe hemodynamic collapse lags the real engine by ~11 h (SBP<100: 37.5 h vs 26.6 h).

studies.name: 04-engine-runtime
studies.title: Engine runtime + cross-engine determinism
studies.question:
Does running the SBML sepsis composite on the Rust viva-core engine instead of
the Python process-bigraph engine produce the same results, and how do their
wall-clock times compare on this real physiology workload?

findings.summary: viva-core drives the real Tellurium process and matches process-bigraph bit-identically.
findings.detail:
viva_core.run drives the real TelluriumProcess via a thin adapter
(viva_simulation_core/analysis/vc_adapter.py) that works around current
viva-core MVP limits (stock address, core injection, empty containers,
map-store overwrites) WITHOUT changing the roadrunner computation. On warm
runs the final state is bit-identical to process-bigraph across all 9
observables (max abs diff 0.0). A fresh-process first roadrunner run differs
by ~1e-6 relative (a Python-side cold-start effect), so the cold tolerance
is rtol=1e-5.

findings.summary: Wall-clock is framework overhead, not a speedup, for this single-heavy-process composite.
findings.detail:
severity 0, 10 s interval, one measurement each (600 s / 3600 s are
simulated time): 600 s -> process-bigraph 25.3 s, viva-core 25.9 s;
3600 s -> process-bigraph 139.9 s, viva-core 125.8 s. Essentially equal, as
predicted: the libroadrunner solver dominates and the tick loop is a small
slice. These single measurements are indicative, not benchmarked.

studies.claim:
viva-core drives the real Tellurium/roadrunner process and reproduces
process-bigraph bit-identically (max abs diff 0.0 across all 9 observables on
warm runs). Wall-clock is essentially equal — a single heavy process means the
engine swap measures framework overhead, not solver time (no ~160x here).

derived.insight: viva-core drives the real Tellurium process and matches process-bigraph bit-identically.
